authority_boundary: This file may guide future authoring and process-golden runtime tests. It may not authorize Q15 release, manuscript release, Core2A eligibility, or learner mastery.
repository_supported_facts: M2D-SBA-23 is titled 'Launch from something already moving'.
Its sole primary Core2 question is Q15.
Its prerequisite buckets are M2D-SBA-03 and M2D-SBA-09.
Core1A/Core2 linkage names Q15 'Moving launch source' and links it to 'moving-launcher'.

learning_atoms.title: Name the frame before naming a velocity
learning_atoms.purpose: Keep platform-relative and ground-relative velocities distinct.
teaching_moves: draw the platform and ground as two labelled frames
attach every velocity arrow to an object and an observer
say velocity of object relative to frame before writing a symbol
misconceptions: a velocity has the same numerical value in every frame
an unlabeled arrow is enough to identify a velocity
checks: label object, observer and velocity on a two-frame sketch

learning_atoms.title: The released object carries the launcher's motion
learning_atoms.purpose: At release, combine the object's velocity relative to the launcher with the launcher's velocity relative to the ground.
teaching_moves: freeze the instant before release
show platform velocity as already present in the ground frame
build v_object,ground = v_object,platform + v_platform,ground vectorially
checks: construct a ground-frame launch vector from two labelled relative velocities

learning_atoms.title: Add vectors before resolving the projectile
learning_atoms.purpose: Form the correct ground-frame initial velocity before applying projectile component equations.
teaching_moves: combine frame velocities first
then resolve the resulting launch vector into x and y components
contrast with resolving each unlabeled speed and adding scalars
misconceptions: projectile equations can start before the reference-frame conversion is complete
checks: state the ground-frame u_x and u_y from a fresh moving-launcher diagram

learning_atoms.title: After release, use one projectile clock
learning_atoms.purpose: Once the ground-frame launch state is known, evolve horizontal and vertical motion on the same time variable.
teaching_moves: mark t=0 at release
write x=u_x t and y=u_y t-1/2 g t^2 for the ground frame when air resistance is neglected
keep the launcher motion separate unless the question explicitly compares them later
misconceptions: the object remains dynamically attached to the launcher after release
horizontal and vertical components use different clocks
checks: write the two ground-frame position equations with one shared t

learning_atoms.title: Gravity does not cancel inherited horizontal motion
learning_atoms.purpose: Separate the post-release gravitational acceleration from the inherited horizontal velocity.
teaching_moves: draw velocity and acceleration arrows immediately after release
show gravity changing only the vertical velocity in the standard model
track horizontal velocity as constant when horizontal acceleration is zero
misconceptions: gravity removes the launcher's horizontal velocity
a downward acceleration implies a downward horizontal component
checks: explain which component gravity changes and which it does not

learning_atoms.title: Choose the observation frame before comparing paths
learning_atoms.purpose: Interpret trajectories consistently when the same release is described from the launcher and from the ground.
teaching_moves: compare two sketches of the same release from different inertial observers
keep the event and clock shared while changing velocity description
distinguish path appearance from physical interaction
misconceptions: different observed paths mean different forces acted
mix coordinates from one frame with velocities from another
checks: identify which quantities must be transformed before using one frame's projectile equations

learning_atoms.title: Check the zero-platform-speed limit
learning_atoms.purpose: Use a limiting case to verify that a moving-launcher model reduces to ordinary projectile motion.
teaching_moves: set platform velocity to zero symbolically
confirm the launch vector becomes the relative launch vector
compare the remaining equations with M2D-SBA-03
misconceptions: a frame-addition formula is valid only when both speeds are nonzero
checks: state what the model becomes when the launcher is stationary

learning_atoms.title: Select the moving-launcher first move
learning_atoms.purpose: Recognise when reference-frame conversion must precede projectile kinematics.
teaching_moves: sort examples into stationary-launch, moving-launcher and moving-observer cases
state the first move before calculating
justify why frame conversion precedes component kinematics
misconceptions: start with a memorised range or flight-time formula before identifying the ground-frame launch velocity
checks: choose and explain the correct first move in an unseen moving-launcher setup

generated_practice.prompt: A trolley moves east at 6 m/s. At one instant a ball is projected at 10 m/s relative to the trolley, 37 degrees above east. Using sin 37 degrees = 0.6 and cos 37 degrees = 0.8, state the ball's initial horizontal and vertical velocity components in the ground frame.
generated_practice.answer_check: Relative components are (8, 6) m/s; add the trolley's (6, 0) m/s, giving ground-frame components (14, 6) m/s.
generated_practice.purpose: Exercise the frame-addition invariant without claiming to reproduce Q15.
